title: The Social World Model Evaluation Gap
abstract: arXiv:2610.33014v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A negotiation assistant can reach a good deal without accurately predicting the other person's response. We ask whether evaluations of social world models test that prediction directly. We audit 113 works published from 1999 to 2026. 9 primary evaluations measure a real person's response to an action selected by the system or experimenter. Only 2 also compare an explicit response forecast with that response. Their predictors use information available when the action is chosen, and the evaluated responses were excluded from fitting; both randomize the intervention. A separate full-text check of 25 language-model works finds no experiment meeting these conditions. The other evaluations test current-state inference, task success, or prediction from recorded actions. We propose a 1-step negotiation experiment that separates these questions. The findings describe the audited sample, not the prevalence of this evaluation gap across the field

translated_title: 社会世界模型评估差距
translated_abstract: 一个谈判助手即使不能准确预测对方的回应，也可以达成一笔好交易。我们探讨社会世界模型的评估是否直接检验这种预测能力。我们审查了1999年至2026年间发表的113篇作品。其中9项主要评估测量了真实的人对系统或实验者所选行动的回应，但只有2项还将明确的回应预测与实际回应进行了比较。它们的预测器使用在选择行动时可获得的信息，且被评估的回应未参与拟合；两者都对干预进行了随机化。对25篇语言模型相关作品的单独全文检查未发现任何符合这些条件的实验。其余评估测试的是当前状态推断、任务成功或基于已记录行动的预测。我们提出了一种单步谈判实验来区分这些问题。这些发现描述的是被审查的样本，而非这种评估差距在整个领域的普遍程度。
tldr: 该研究审查了113篇文献后发现，社会世界模型的评估很少直接检验模型对真人回应的预测能力，25篇语言模型相关作品中甚至没有一项实验符合直接预测评估的条件，为此作者提出一种单步谈判实验来填补这一评估空白。
en_tdlr: An audit of 113 publications reveals that social world model evaluations rarely directly test the models' ability to predict real people's responses to chosen actions—with no language-model experiment meeting these criteria—prompting the authors to propose a 1-step negotiation experiment to address this evaluation gap.
